about.subtitle: Talk To Paste · v{{version}}
about.description: TTP is a free, open-source app I built because I got tired of typing. Press your hotkey, talk, your words land in whatever you're using. Groq does the transcription. An optional polish pass trims the 'uhms'.
about.author: Built by Amir KELLOU--SIDHOUM. If you find it useful, feel free to share it or connect with me!
about.privacyBody: TTP collects none of your data. Your API key is stored locally on your machine. Audio is sent directly from your device to Groq's servers for transcription. I never see, store, or have access to any of it. Same for AI Polish: your text goes straight to Groq, not through me. Everything stays between you and your API provider.

pro.title: Support TTP
pro.descFree: TTP is free and complete — every feature, no limits, no subscription. If it saves you time and you feel like sending something back, a one-off licence is a way to do that. It unlocks nothing; you already have everything.
pro.deactivateHelp: Deactivating frees an activation slot so you can use this license on another device.

companion.faceDesc: Two marks that blink when nothing is happening, hold still while it works, and mark the moment your words land. Every variety is subtle by default, and none of them ever ask you for anything.

house.name: House
house.desc: The one it was born with. You stop seeing it around the third day, and you would notice if it left.

shut.name: Shut
shut.desc: Eyes closed until you press the key. Everything it has is in the fifth of a second where they open.

drowsy.name: Drowsy
drowsy.desc: Heavy lids, a long slow blink, and always a beat behind you. It never once startles you.

quick.name: Quick
quick.desc: Short sharp blinks, often two at a time. Good company for a four-second dictation and bad company for an afternoon of writing.

bead.name: Bead
bead.desc: Two small dots set as wide as the body allows. Still for ten seconds, two blinks, still again.

default.name: House
default.desc: The two polite tones TTP was born with.

bowl.name: Bowl
bowl.desc: A small brass bowl. The stop is someone's hand on it.

marimba.name: Marimba
marimba.desc: Two notes on a wooden bar. Up to begin, down to finish.

submarine.name: Submarine
submarine.desc: A sonar ping into the quiet. Something down there heard it.

felt.name: Felt
felt.desc: A piano with a blanket over it. Barely a sound at all.

bubble.name: Bubble
bubble.desc: A drop going in, and a drop coming back out.

notes.3-1-7:
TTP is free. Every feature, uncapped, no account, no trial that runs out.
• The Companion: the pill has a face, and TTP has sound packs — bowl, marimba, felt. Cosmetic and nothing else: no sound and no face changes what TTP does with your voice.
• AI Polish works again. Groq decommissioned the model we were using on 16 August; we migrated, and every attempt is now timed so the next outage announces itself instead of looking like a slow model.
• Dead microphone: if your headset is connected but streaming nothing, TTP says so after two seconds — while you can still do something about it — instead of letting you talk into it for twenty and losing the lot.
• The microphone can no longer be left on. A capture that finishes starting after you have already let go of the key is now refused rather than left running with nobody to close it.
• Faster: the macOS keychain no longer sits between your last word and your text. One read measured 62 seconds was waiting there.
• The Fn key survives: when macOS disables our keyboard tap and re-arming it stops helping, we rebuild it.
• Diagnostics: every dictation now leaves a stage-by-stage trace in ttp-trace.log. Settings → Advanced → Diagnostics.
notes.3-1-6: Fix: even the minimal "French and English bilingual speaker." prompt was leaking at the end of transcriptions on trailing silence (Whisper copied the prompt tail and started a continuation). Radical fix: we no longer send ANY prompt to Whisper. Language is handled by the `language` API parameter, proper-noun correction by the post-transcription word-boundary pass which can never add words that weren't already present. Zero prompt-bias risk going forward.
notes.3-1-5:
Explicit transcription-language picker + bigger WASAPI drain.
• Settings → Transcription → "Transcription language": explicit
Auto / English / French dropdown. Before, we silently followed the
UI language — a French speaker using TTP in English would get their
French audio mis-transcribed. Auto lets Whisper detect (recommended
for bilingual use), pinning forces a specific language.
• WASAPI drain bumped 200ms → 400ms before tearing down the cpal
stream. The 200ms wasn't always enough on Windows drivers with
larger internal buffers (reported cutoff was longer than a typical
trailing buffer). 400ms gives headroom for the slowest observed
configurations.
notes.3-1-4:
Two field-reported bugs from v3.1.3-1 fixed:
• Trailing words / last syllable are no longer cut off. WASAPI (Windows) holds up to 150ms of captured audio in its internal buffer between the device and the cpal callback. We were dropping the stream immediately on key release, losing that trailing buffer. Added a 200ms drain delay before tearing the stream down — you recover your last syllable / word.
• Dictionary words no longer appear pasted onto the end of your messages. We were passing the proper-noun list inline in the Whisper prompt to help with recognition — Whisper occasionally regurgitated those nouns at the end of legitimate transcriptions (classic prompt-bias trailing-token leak). The prompt is now minimal ('French and English bilingual speaker.'). Proper-noun correction still happens, just through the post-transcription word-boundary dictionary pass, which never adds words that weren't already in the transcription.
notes.3-1-3: Fix: Whisper hallucinated sentences like "Glossary, c'est une phrase très importante." on silent recordings. Root cause: the prompt we send Whisper to bias toward dictionary proper nouns literally started with "Glossary:" — the decoder picked up the word and wrote a sentence ABOUT glossaries. We dropped the introducer from the prompt (proper nouns are now sent without any introducer word) and added a safety net that filters "Glossary,..." / "Glossaire,..." leading short recordings (≤ 6 s, ≤ 8 words).
notes.3-1-2:
Four fixes from v3.1.1-1 field reports:
• Spam-clicking the tray Record button no longer leaves the app stuck in "Recording". 300ms debounce on tray clicks + audio_capture self-heals a stale state instead of returning "recording_already_in_progress".
• Whisper no longer returns Chinese / Russian / Korean transcriptions on silent stretches: the decoder is now pinned to your UI language (en/fr) instead of per-frame auto-detection.
• Whisper no longer hallucinates "thank you" on silent recordings: pre-API RMS check, if the audio is effectively silent we skip Whisper and surface "no speech detected".
• Hallucination filter now catches "Sous-titré par <studio>", "Captions by X", "Untertitel von X" and other subtitle-credit stems Whisper bleeds onto short noisy clips.
notes.3-1-1: Fix: a Ctrl+Space double-tap could leave the app stuck in a "Processing" state from which every subsequent shortcut press was a no-op (reported by a user on v3.1.0-1, Windows). Every error path in process_audio now resets state to Idle before bubbling up, and the double-tap detector now clears its timestamp so the next tap isn't misread as the third tap of a triple-tap.
notes.3-1-0:
Big update: VAD auto-stop, mic picker, one-click history re-paste, hands-free indicator on the pill.
• Auto-stop after silence (opt-in): ends the recording automatically once you've stopped speaking. Useful when you forget to release Fn. Tunable 1-10 seconds in Settings → Behavior.
• Input device picker: pick the mic to record from explicitly (helpful with AirPods + built-in mic). If your chosen device is unplugged, TTP falls back to the system default automatically.
• Re-paste a past transcription: open Settings → History, hover a row, click the Repeat icon → the entry is typed back into the focused app.
• Hands-free visual cue: a small lock icon now shows on the pill when you're in hands-free mode, as a reminder that a single tap stops the session.
• Hard 5-minute recording ceiling: protects against a hands-free session you forgot about overnight.
• Under the hood: Sentry now captures real Rust panics (they used to disappear silently), settings.json is written atomically (no more corruption on kill), one shared cpal audio stream instead of two (kills the #1 cause of "silent recording" reports on some drivers), more honest privacy copy throughout.
notes.3-0-4:
More reliable mic capture + clearer no-speech signals.
• Replaced the third-party mic-recorder plugin with our in-house cpal capture. No more empty 68-byte WAVs when mic permission was silently revoked after an update (root cause of the "nothing captured" reports in v3.0.x).
• The no-speech path is hardened: if Whisper returns empty text or a known Whisper hallucination, we filter it cleanly with a targeted message instead of a generic error toast.
• No action needed. Your shortcuts, key, and preferences carry over.
notes.3-0-3:
Guided nudge for the Globe key emoji picker.
• If you use Fn to talk but macOS pops the emoji picker instead, TTP now offers a step-by-step guide to switch Globe to "No action" under System Settings → Keyboard.
• The nudge shows once and stays dismissable. No-op if Fn already works.
notes.3-0-2:
Fn emoji-picker fix + single-tap hands-free stop.
• On macOS Sequoia, pressing Fn sometimes launched the emoji picker instead of recording. Patched at the event-tap layer: we consume the event before the system routes it to the IME.
• In hands-free mode, a single Fn tap now ends the session (was: had to double-tap to exit).
